Four competing telehealth platforms filed coordinated federal lobbying registrations in May 2026, signaling industry-wide mobilization around prescription economics and telehealth access policy. This competitor activity typically precedes state-level regulatory consolidation around anti-kickback and fee-splitting enforcement, particularly in high-population states where Zocdoc maintains material user volume. Industry-standard regulatory exposures for this business model include state medical board review of advertising claims tied to prescriber credentials and consumer protection scrutiny of patient-routing economic incentives.
